<hypothesis>
To discriminate broadly, I should vary catalyst concentration significantly. High catalyst loading amplifies effects that are second-order in catalyst:
- M2, M3 (catalyst dimerization equilibrium): rate saturates or decreases with [cat]
- M13, M19 (irreversible catalyst dimerization to inactive): deactivation accelerates
- M5 (catS + cat → catP + cat): rate increases super-linearly in cat
- M6, M8 (cat activation): different scaling

High [cat] with moderate [S] will also quickly consume substrate, letting us see late-time behavior (deactivation pathways M9, M11, M14, M18, M20 reveal themselves via incomplete conversion).

Using high catalyst loading (0.1 M) with moderate substrate (1.0 M) probes multiple effects: dimerization, deactivation pathways, and super-linear catalyst dependence. This is maximally informative across many mechanistic classes.
</hypothesis>
